findings.how: Round 1: an eye icon, title= with the full text, a full-width line from the start, and state words on the target chip. Round 2 (de27370): a crowded line gives way in order. findings.how: Round 1: a right-click in the field opens Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all; Return and ⌃⇧⌘ glyph chords on a Mac. Round 2 (09b9c0a): AskWindow notes a blur that comes while the menu is up; a focus clears it. When the menu closes, the callback gives the OS 120 ms to say where the keyboard went, and a blur in that time closes the box as usual. After that the box keeps the keyboard, takes it back if nothing else took it, or, after such a blur, goes away instead of calling focus().

Under Xvfb with and without mutter (scratch rclick-away.cjs), Paste still lands in the box, and a click on an xterm only closes the GTK menu (no blur, the box keeps the keyboard), as before. ember-win32.test.ts adds a real-runner check.

findings.how: 99e6445 adds the probe the verifier asked for to the real-runner suites. ember-win32.test.ts starts the built Ember as at login and presses Win+Alt+Space through SendInput. ember-darwin.test.ts presses ⌃⇧⌘Space as CGEvents. Each lets go of the keys, types "quick brown fox" at 40 ms a letter, and prints what the box holds and what that decides: nothing lost means telling users to let go of the keys before typing is enough; letters lost means the OS needs a typed-ahead hold. A run fails only if the chord doesn't open the box, or the box holds letters out of order. DEVELOPING.md's suite table describes it. Still open until those runs report: the native hold or the documented sentence (handed to docs below).
findings.test: typeahead-probe.test.ts covers the verdict, and tsc covers the suites. The probes run only on windows-2022 and macos-15.

verifierProblems.what: Plausible on Windows and macOS; I couldn't check it here. While the right-click menu is up, the box ignores blur (menuUp). The popup callback then calls win.focus() whenever the box isn't focused. If the user dismisses the menu by clicking another app, the box doesn't close, and it can take focus back from that app once the menu has closed. On Windows that click can also activate the other window. On Linux under GTK, I confirmed with and without mutter that the box stays focused and Paste works.
verifierProblems.fix: In editMenu, note whether a blur arrived while the menu was up.
